omissions.fact: The candidate has personal backend project experience, but no backend job experience.
omissions.source_quote: no backend job experience, only my own projects
omissions.why_it_matters: An explicitly labelled personal-project reference would provide the only available evidence of backend exposure for this full-stack role, without inventing languages, frameworks or professional experience.

requirements.requirement: 2+ years of professional React and TypeScript web application development
Node.js backend services and SQL databases
Semantic HTML, responsive layouts and accessibility basics
Automated unit and end-to-end testing and Git workflows
Authentication, OWASP fundamentals and willingness to learn health-data privacy
Next.js or another server-side rendering framework
AWS or similar cloud and Docker
Mentor interns or junior colleagues when opportunities arise
requirements.evidence_quote: Supported approximately 30 first-year students during one semester of web development labs.

fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents honestly present an early-career applicant and keep student work separate from professional employment. They do not fabricate the required stack or experience, but leave most technical requirements unaddressed and omit the available personal backend-project exposure. The teaching experience is a useful, appropriately scoped analogue for mentoring.

issues: No email address, telephone number or other contact channel is supplied; none was available in the candidate material.
No technical skills section or project technology details establish suitability for the advertised stack. Those details cannot safely be invented.
No education details, institution names or project links are available or included.
Each dated experience category has only one entry, so chronology within categories is valid; the overall section order prioritises the 2024 project ahead of the 2025 teaching role.
The GraphQL course receives both profile and learning-section space despite having little relevance to this advertisement.

reasons: The single-column PDF extracts cleanly and uses recognisable section headings.
There is no evidence of the mandatory React/TypeScript professional experience or the backend, database and testing stack.
The two matching development terms appear as interests, not demonstrated technical qualifications.
The missing named technologies are not established by the candidate's notes, so inserting them would be unjustified.

issues: Company tailoring is limited to patient experience, accessibility and privacy; it does not connect a specific product or engineering practice to concrete candidate evidence.
The letter repeats nearly all the CV's limited content, including the relatively irrelevant GraphQL course.
It offers no evidence of React, TypeScript, Node.js, SQL or testing and omits the candidate's personal backend projects.
The substantial experience mismatch is signalled through early-career wording but not directly explained.
strengths: Names Verdane Care and the correct Patient Experience role.
Uses accurate company priorities without claiming healthcare or accessibility expertise.
Clearly distinguishes student project experience from professional work.
Connects teaching assistance to communication and collaboration without inflating it into leadership.
Concise, courteous and free from stale employer references.

spacing_issues: Both pages leave substantial lower-page whitespace, especially the cover letter; this reflects limited content rather than pagination failure.
issues: The CV has a clear hierarchy, aligned dates and consistent section rules, but the name-only header lacks a practical contact block.
The letter is visually plain but coherent with the CV's serif typography.

fluency_and_tone_issues: 'collaborative hackathon delivery' is compressed, abstract wording for a straightforward student team project.
'continuing to develop across frontend and full-stack work' is vague; clearer wording would describe developing frontend and backend skills.

notes_facts_used: Second place in a 2024 student hackathon.
Three-person team, 24-hour duration and responsibility for the transit notifier frontend.
One semester as a first-year web development teaching assistant in spring 2025, helping approximately 30 students.
Free online GraphQL course, explicitly not yet applied in a project.
Interest in junior frontend or full-stack development.
Social-media volunteering for a sea swimming club.
notes_facts_ignored: Personal backend projects and absence of backend job experience.

evaluation.summary: These are clean, readable and factually restrained documents that preserve the distinction between student experience, introductory learning and professional work. The hackathon and teaching achievements are accurately quantified, and the letter names the correct employer and role. However, the application establishes almost none of the required technical stack or professional experience, and it misses the available personal backend-project exposure. Missing contact details also weaken its practical usability, although the supplied material contained none.
